payload.set_intro: Two students pull on the same sled of mass $20\text{ kg}$ that rests on frictionless ice. One student pulls with a constant horizontal force of $90\text{ N}$ due east and the other pulls with a constant horizontal force of $50\text{ N}$ due north. No other horizontal force acts on the sled.

stimulus.description: Two students pull on the same sled of mass $20\text{ kg}$ that rests on frictionless ice. One student pulls with a constant horizontal force of $90\text{ N}$ due east and the other pulls with a constant horizontal force of $50\text{ N}$ due north. No other horizontal force acts on the sled.

items.stem: What is the magnitude of the net force on the sled?

options.why: Averages the two forces.
Subtracts the smaller force from the larger one, as if they were opposite.
The two forces are perpendicular, so the magnitude of the net force is $\sqrt{F_1^2+F_2^2}=\sqrt{(90)^2+(50)^2}=103\text{ N}$.
Reports only the larger of the two forces.

items.explanation_en:
The correct answer is $103\text{ N}$. The two forces are perpendicular, so the magnitude of the net force is $\sqrt{F_1^2+F_2^2}=\sqrt{(90)^2+(50)^2}=103\text{ N}$.
$70.0\text{ N}$ is incorrect: Averages the two forces.
$40.0\text{ N}$ is incorrect: Subtracts the smaller force from the larger one, as if they were opposite.
$90.0\text{ N}$ is incorrect: Reports only the larger of the two forces.

items.stem: What is the magnitude of the acceleration of the sled?
